papers.title: Polynomial Swap Coboundary Expansion with Applications to LTCs and PCPs
papers.abstract: Swap coboundary expansion, introduced independently by Bafna--Minzer and Dikstein--Dinur, is a local-to-global property that underlies agreement tests in the low-acceptance regime and recent constructions of succinct PCPs. Previous works obtained bounds of $\exp(-O(\sqrt{r}))$ for the $r$-swap coboundary expansion of Chapman--Lubotzky complexes. We establish the first inverse-polynomial bounds for bounded-degree complexes: suitable skeleta of Kac--Moody--Steinberg (KMS) complexes have $r$-swap coboundary expansion at least $r^{-O(1)}$. Our theorem supplies a key ingredient in forthcoming work of Ben Yaacov--Dikstein--Liu, which obtains local tests for sparse algebraic codes with guarantees even at arbitrarily small acceptance probability. These tests use $\exp(\operatorname{poly}(1/\varepsilon))$ queries and guarantee that any word accepted with probability at least $\varepsilon$ agrees with a codeword on an $\varepsilon^{O(1)}$ fraction of coordinates. Separately, substituting our bound into the existing analysis of Bafna--Minzer--Vyas--Yun improves the soundness dependence of their two-query PCP construction, giving perfect completeness, soundness $\varepsilon$, and proof length $n(\log n)^{\exp(\operatorname{poly}(1/\varepsilon))}$. Our proof exploits the product structure of the groups arising in KMS complexes. The main new ingredient is a decomposition lemma for Dehn functions, which separates the analysis of group relations into independent problems on much smaller factors, with only polynomial overhead.

papers.title: Half-factorial generating sets and the realization of Dedekind class groups
papers.abstract: We prove a cardinality obstruction to realizing an abelian group as the ideal class group of a half-factorial Dedekind domain. If an abelian $p$-group $P$ satisfies $\bigcap_{r\ge1}p^rP=0$ and admits a half-factorial generating subset, then $|P|\le\max\{\aleph_0,|P/pP|\}$. The proof separates generators of equal order by finite quotients. Its group-theoretic ingredient is a direct summand generated by selected members of an arbitrary finite generating set. The torsion subgroup of $\prod_{j\ge1}\mathbb{Z}/p^j\mathbb{Z}$ is uncountable and $p$-adically separated, but has countable quotient modulo $p$; hence it has no half-factorial generating subset. This gives a negative answer to the universal half-factorial Dedekind realization problem for every prime. Pure subgroups give counterexamples of every uncountable cardinality at most the continuum, so the least cardinality of a counterexample is $\aleph_1$. We also study free-kernel lifting, order-preserving lifts across torsion kernels, character-compatible generators, and the failure of compatibility under unions and contraction. These results distinguish global realizability from half-factoriality on bounded subgroups and from integrality of cross numbers.

papers.title: The unitary group $U_3(4)$ as a Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$
papers.abstract: We prove that the simple unitary group $U_3(4)=\operatorname{PSU}_3(\mathbb{F}_4)$, of order $62400$, is the Galois group of a regular extension of $\mathbb{Q}(t)$, and hence of infinitely many extensions of $\mathbb{Q}$. The extension has four branch points, with inertia groups of orders $2$, $2$, $3$, $3$, and it is the only extension with these properties up to a rational change of the coordinate $t$. We give an explicit polynomial of degree $65$ for it.

papers.title: Symmetric Chemical Reaction Networks: Realizations and Steady States
papers.abstract: We investigate symmetric chemical reaction networks and their steady states. From classical equivariant dynamical systems and network theory it is known that the mass- action ODE of any symmetric chemical reaction network is equivariant. For symmetries that permute the species, we prove that any equivariant mass-action ODE is realized by a symmetric chemical reaction network and construct a sparsest such realization. We apply the half-degree principle to show that a symmetric CRN that has a steady state also has one with few distinct coordinates.

papers.title: Intervals in affine Bruhat order
papers.abstract: Let $(W,S)$ be an irreducible affine Coxeter system. We study Bruhat intervals in $W$ via the well-known characterization of Bruhat order in terms of galleries. We start by using folded galleries to formulate an analogous order on the coweight lattice, which we call Iwahori order. This allows us to reduce the description of certain Bruhat intervals to that of the corresponding Iwahori intervals. We next give closed-form descriptions of all Iwahori intervals, using the quantum Bruhat graph (QBG). More precisely, we show that lower Iwahori intervals saturate pseudo-Weyl polytopes (that is, certain intersections of negative cones), and upper Iwahori intervals saturate certain unions of positive cones, with the cone points given by explicit formulae involving paths in the QBG. We then describe arbitrary Bruhat intervals by partitioning them into their core, a large region which is (in most cases) completely determined by an Iwahori interval, and their crust, the complementary boundary region. We conclude by proving that, under a super-regularity assumption, the crust is covered by certain locally-defined tesselating shapes. All statements and proofs are rank- and type-free.

papers.title: Lau's Fixed Point Problem for Elementary Amenable Groups and Finite Left Amenable Semigroups
papers.abstract: Lau's fixed point conjecture is proved for elementary amenable groups. More generally, a weak$^*$-continuous nonexpansive representation of such a group on a nonempty weak$^*$-closed nonexpansive retract of a weak$^*$-compact convex subset $C$ of a dual Banach space has a nonempty common fixed point set that is a nonexpansive retract of $C$. For finite left amenable semigroups, continuity and weak$^*$-closedness of the retract are unnecessary. The argument also leads to a new class of amenable groups with the same retraction property, which contains all elementary amenable groups and may be strictly larger. This class may provide a useful framework for further research on Lau's conjecture. Bruck's theorem is also extended from abelian to elementary amenable group actions on nonexpansive retracts of weakly compact convex sets with the fixed point and conditional fixed point properties, without weak continuity, thus partially answering a longstanding question of Bruck. Several consequences of the theorem are recorded.

papers.title: Minimal Models for Free Quasi-Invariant and Stationary Actions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we generalize the fact that essentially free p.m.p. actions of a countably infinite group admit a minimal model, proved by Weiss and Zucker. We prove that minimal models exist for every essentially free non singular action. Furthermore, as in the p.m.p. case, we prove that all essentially free $\mu$-stationary actions (with respect to a fixed generating probability measure $\mu$) admit a common minimal model.

papers.title: Regular subgroups of wreath products and Cayley Cartesian products
papers.abstract: The Cartesian product of Cayley graphs is again a Cayley graph. For connected graphs, the converse question reduces to Cartesian powers of Cartesian-prime graphs, and consequently to the study of regular subgroups of wreath products in the product action. We prove that, for a transitive permutation group $G$ of degree $2p$ or $4p$, where $p$ is prime, $G\wr S_2$ contains a regular subgroup if and only if $G$ does, and construct counterexamples of degree $8p$ for every prime $p\equiv3\pmod4$. By modifying this construction, we obtain an infinite family of connected non-Cayley graphs whose Cartesian squares are Cayley graphs, giving a negative answer to the converse question. The smallest graph in our family has $120$ vertices and valency $27$. In contrast, we prove that a connected vertex-transitive graph of order $pq$, where $p$ and $q$ are primes, has a Cayley Cartesian power if and only if the graph itself is Cayley.

papers.title: Orbital graph structure of alternating full groups and simple torsion amenable groups of exponential growth
papers.abstract: We develop a framework for constructing simple alternating full groups A(G, X), associated with finite fragmentations of minimal expansive dihedral Cantor actions, with controlled orbital-graph codings and purely non-Hausdorff singularities. We also prove that positive entropy of a naturally labeled admissible orbital line forces exponential word growth of the acting group. As an application, we construct continuum many pairwise abstractly nonisomorphic, finitely generated, infinite, simple, torsion, amenable groups of exponential word growth. They arise as alternating full groups of fragmented minimal expansive dihedral Cantor actions with linearly repetitive generic regular orbital graphs and purely non-Hausdorff singularities. Under the same minimality, expansivity, linear repetitivity and singularity assumptions, if every finite clopen coding is determined by a bounded fragmentation window, the alternating full group has intermediate word growth.

papers.title: A notion of pseudo-morphisms with applications to the study of polynomial maps and of link-homotopy groups of 2-string link
papers.abstract: We introduce a notion of pseudo-morphism for groups, which extends the notion of group morphism from a group to a ring. We show that pseudo-morphisms from a group $G$ to an integral domain $R$ form a filtred Hopf algebra which can be seen as an efficient notion of dual for $G$. We also show that pseudo-morphisms are closely related to the notion of polynomial maps in the sense of Eilenberg-MacLane/Passi, the two notions even coinciding when $G$ is finitely generated and $R$ is a field. It follows that, in that case, polynomial maps are endowed with an Hopf structure. In a second part, we study non repeated Milnor invariants (in the $4$-dimensional context of $2$-string links) from this pseudo-morphism point of view. We show that they form a sub-bialgebra of the Hopf algebra of pseudo-morphisms on the group of $2$-string links up to link-homotopy, and prove that it is isomorphic to an explicit quotient $\textrm{Mil}$ of a polynomial ring. This leads to a fully algebraic description of the group of 2-string links up to link-homotopy as the dual group associated to $\textrm{Mil}$. As a by-product, we obtain that non repeated Milnor invariants are polynomial maps, and we show that this can be used to give a new proof of their finite type property.

papers.title: Finite generation of the second homology group of the genus three Torelli group
papers.abstract: We prove that the group $H_2(\mathcal{I}_3;\mathbb{Z})$ is finitely generated, where $\mathcal{I}_3$ is the Torelli subgroup of the mapping class group of a closed genus-three surface $\Sigma_3$. A key role in the proof is played by establishing the following property: for each symplectic transvection $t_x\in\mathrm{Sp}_{6}(\mathbb{Z})$, we have $$ \bigl(t^{120}_x-1\bigr)^{57}\bigl(t_x^{24}-1\bigr)(t_x-1)^6H_2(\mathcal{I}_3;\mathbb{Z})=0. $$ The proof is based on the study of the spectral sequences associated with the action of $\mathcal{I}_3$ on the Bestvina-Bux-Margalit complex of minimizing cycles and with the actions on certain auxiliary complexes of the stabilizers of two- and three-component multicurves on $\Sigma_3$. The remaining ingredients are Tavgen's theorem, which asserts that $\mathrm{Sp}_{6}(\mathbb{Z})$ has bounded elementary generation, and the result of Kassabov and Putman, which asserts that $H_2(\mathcal{I}_3;\mathbb{Z})$ is finitely generated as a $\mathbb{Z}[\mathrm{Sp}_6(\mathbb{Z})]$-module.

papers.title: Centralizers in Catalan Monoids
papers.abstract: Fix a chain $X_n=\{1<\cdots<n\}$, where $n$ is a positive integer. The Catalan monoid $\mathcal{C}_n$ consists of all decreasing and order-preserving transformations of $X_n$, with function composition as the operation. For $\beta\in\mathcal{C}_n$, its centralizer is $C(\beta)=\{\alpha\in\mathcal{C}_n:\alpha\beta=\beta\alpha\}$. We characterize the elements of $C(\varepsilon)$, $C(\mu)$, and $C(\beta)$, where $\varepsilon\in\mathcal{C}_n$ is an idempotent, $\mu\in\mathcal{C}_n$ is a nilpotent, and $\beta\in\mathcal{C}_n$ is a general element. For an idempotent $\varepsilon\in\mathcal{C}_n$, we derive formulas for the cardinality of $C(\varepsilon)$, as well as formulas for the numbers of idempotents and nilpotents of $C(\varepsilon)$. We relate indexing sets arising in these formulas to Dyck paths and Narayana numbers. For a nilpotent $\mu\in\mathcal{C}_n$, we present algorithms that construct $C(\mu)$, its subset of idempotents, and its subsemigroup of nilpotents, thereby determining their cardinalities. We also describe the nilpotents whose centralizers consist only of idempotents, of nilpotents together with the identity, or of nilpotents and idempotents. We extend these descriptions to arbitrary elements of $\mathcal{C}_n$. To obtain our results, we represent $\beta\in\mathcal{C}_n$ as a sequence $\langle T_1,\ldots,T_m\rangle$ of rooted trees. The sets of vertices of the trees form a partition of $X_n$. Each tree is level-ordered, which means that it can be drawn in such a way that moving from the root down, level by level, from left to right at each level, we pass through an increasing sequence of consecutive elements of $X_n$.

papers.title: Expansion in powers of simple groups of Lie type
papers.abstract: We prove an expansion theorem for direct powers of all nonabelian finite simple groups $G$ other than the alternating groups and the Suzuki groups ${}^2B_2(q)$. If $G^m$ is generated by $d\ge2$ elements, then $G^m$ has a symmetric generating multiset of at most $Cd$ elements and normalized spectral gap at least $C^{-1}d^{-\log_2 3}$, for an absolute constant $C>0$. In particular, this answers a question of Sabatini on $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)^p$. For $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$, we use the expander graphs constructed by Lubotzky--Samuels--Vishne, and an amplification trick for direct powers; in high rank, we use the Ershov--Jaikin-Zapirain property (T) theorem.

papers.title: On complemented skew braces
papers.abstract: We investigate complemented skew left braces, that is, skew braces in which every skew subbrace admits a complement. We establish that if every minimal subbrace of a finite skew brace is complemented, then the brace is supersoluble and all its skew subbraces of prime power order are elementary abelian. We also show that the converse does not hold in general, providing a finite counterexample. Furthermore, we prove that every subbrace of a finite direct product of square-free skew braces is complemented. Finally, we extend our investigation to the infinite setting, proving that every multipermutational complemented skew brace is hypercyclic and that all its skew subbraces whose additive groups are $p$-groups are elementary abelian.

papers.title: On Block-Primitive Combinatorial Designs
papers.abstract: We settle a long-standing problem by proving that every block-primitive combinatorial design is point-primitive. Since block-primitivity and point-primitivity coincide for symmetric designs by duality, it remains to treat the non-symmetric $2$-designs. For these we apply the O'Nan--Scott theorems for primitive and for quasiprimitive permutation groups and prove that the automorphism group of every such design is almost simple on points and on blocks. Together with the classification of finite simple groups, this classifies all non-symmetric block-primitive $2$-designs except for two families of block stabilizers in even characteristic. The exceptions are as follows. One family is of subfield type, $PSL_2(q_0)$ with $q=q_0^{d}$, $d\geq2$, of order below the dihedral point stabilizer $D_{2(q\pm1)}$, and includes $S_3\cong PSL_2(2)$ and $A_5\cong PSL_2(4)$. The other is the dihedral block stabilizer $D_{2(q-1)}$, where the block is a union of $a$ of the $q/2$ orbits, so that $v=q(q-1)/2$, $k=a(q-1)$ and $\lambda=2a(aq-a-1)/(q-2)$, the last an integer exactly when $(q-2)/2$ divides $a(a-1)$; this family is exhausted by finite enumeration except at the degrees beyond its range. We then determine which of these designs have strength $t\geq 3$. Apart from the inversive planes and the five Witt designs, exactly two Steiner families arise, attached to the exceptional maximal subgroups of $PGL_2(q)$. There is no non-complete design of strength $t\geq 6$.

papers.title: A counterexample to the subgraphings approximate the cost problem
papers.abstract: We prove that for every $k\ge 2$, the free group $\mathbb{F}_k$ on $k$ generators admits a finite generating set $S$ such that the Schreier graphing of the Bernoulli action of $\mathbb{F}_k$ with respect to $S$ does not admit spanning subgraphings that would approximate the cost of the action. In particular, this gives an example of a graphing that spans a treeable countable pmp equivalence relation, but does not admit a spanning subtreeing.

papers.title: The monoid of orientation preserving mappings on a chain
papers.abstract: We introduce new kinds of regular monoids of transformations consisting of mappings which preserve or reverse the orientation of a finite cycle.

papers.title: Average character degree below 14/3
papers.abstract: We prove that a finite group with average irreducible character degree less than $14/3$ is solvable if it has no chief factor isomorphic to $A_5$. This answers a question of Aziziheris and Eivazzadeh.

papers.title: Finite presentations for Thompson monoids
papers.abstract: Thompson's group $V$ was introduced in 1965 as one of the first examples of an infinite finitely presented simple group. The Higman-Thompson groups $V_{k, r}$ naturally generalize $V$; they exhibit many of the same interesting properties and have been extensively studied in the literature. Monoid theoretic analogues $TV_{k, r}$, $PTV_{k, r}$, and $IV_{k, r}$ of the Higman-Thompson groups were first considered by Thompson, and published many years later in work of Birget. The monoid theoretic analogue of the symmetric group is the full transformation monoid, in that every monoid is isomorphic to a submonoid of some full transformation monoid. The analogous role for inverse monoids is played by the symmetric inverse monoid. Birget's three monoids $TV_{k, r}$, $PTV_{k, r}$, and $IV_{k, r}$ are to $V_{n, r}$ what the full, and partial transformation monoids, and the symmetric inverse monoid are to the symmetric group. The second author and De Witt recently showed that $TV_{k, r}$ is finitely presented. In this paper we show that the remaining two monoids $PTV_{k, r}$ and $IV_{k, r}$ are also finitely presented.

papers.title: Kronecker Coefficients and Simultaneous Conjugacy Classes
papers.abstract: A Kronecker coefficient is the multiplicity of an irreducible representation of a finite group $G$ in a tensor product of irreducible representations. We define Kronecker Hecke algebras and use them as a tool to study Kronecker coefficients in finite groups. We show that the number of simultaneous conjugacy classes in a finite group $G$ is equal to the sum of squares of Kronecker coefficients, and the number of simultaneous conjugacy classes that are closed under elementwise inversion is the sum of Kronecker coefficients weighted by Frobenius-Schur indicators. We use these tools to investigate which finite groups have multiplicity-free tensor products. We introduce the class of doubly real groups, and show that they are precisely the real groups which have multiplicity-free tensor products. We show that non-Abelian groups of odd order, non-Abelian finite simple groups, and most finite general linear groups do not have multiplicity-free tensor products.

papers.title: 2-generation of Chevalley Lie algebras over finite fields
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove that every split simple Chevalley Lie algebra over a finite field of characteristic $p\neq 2$ of classical types $B_n$, $C_n$, and $D_n$, and exceptional types $G_2$, $F_4$, $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$, is $2$-generated. Combined with the result of Cantor, Jezernik, and Zozaya for the classical type $A_n$ [Two-generation of traceless matrices over finite fields, Linear Algebra Appl. (2025)], this establishes $2$-generation for all split simple Chevalley Lie algebras over finite fields of characteristic $p\neq 2$.

papers.title: Completeness of closed Kleinian flat Pseudo-Riemannian Manifolds of Signature (2,2)
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{R}^{2,2}$ denote the model space of flat pseudo-Riemannian manifolds of signature $(2,2)$. We prove that the only domain divisible by a discrete subgroup of the isometry group of $\mathbb{R}^{2,2}$ is $\mathbb{R}^{2,2}$ itself. In the Kleinian setting, this provides the first completeness theorem of closed flat pseudo-Riemannian manifolds beyond the Euclidean and Lorentzian cases. Along the proof, we show as a result of independent interest concerning the existence of syndetic hulls in semidirect products $R \ltimes G$, where $G$ is a homothety Lie group. This construction generalizes earlier constructions in affine geometry due to Carri\`ere and Dal'bo.

papers.title: The set of numerical semigroups of a given multiplicity and Frobenius number
papers.abstract: We study the structure of the family of numerical semigroups with fixed multiplicity and Frobenius number. We give an algorithmic method to compute all the semigroups in this family. As an application we compute the set of all numerical semigroups with given multiplicity and genus.

papers.title: Embeddability of right-angled Artin groups into hierarchically hyperbolic groups
papers.abstract: For a hierarchically hyperbolic group, we give sufficient conditions ensuring that suitable powers of a finite collection of elements generate a right-angled Artin subgroup; under an additional condition, this subgroup is undistorted. We verify these hypotheses in two natural situations: one modeled on mapping class groups, using structural assumptions on the ambient HHG, and one modeled on RAAGs, requiring the chosen elements to be rigidly fully supported. Our results recover known embedding theorems for mapping class groups and extend the non-annular undistortion theorem of Clay--Leininger--Mangahas, while also recovering the Kim--Koberda extension graph theorem for RAAGs.

papers.title: Rank 1 phenomena for groups of positive deficiency
papers.abstract: We examine second bounded cohomology and mod p homology in finite index subgroups of 1-relator groups and groups with a presentation of positive deficiency. We use this to determine exactly which subgroups of 1-relator groups are boundedly generated.

papers.title: Dynamics of Dehn twists in the outer automorphism group of a free group
papers.abstract: We study Dehn twists in the outer automorphism group of a free group through the doubled handlebody, a connected sum of copies of the product of a circle and a two-sphere, in which the Dehn twist along a primitive torus is induced by twisting a regular neighborhood of the torus. Our main result states that sufficiently large powers of the Dehn twists along a compatible collection of primitive tori generate a right-angled Artin group. The proof is a ping-pong argument in the universal cover, the complement of a Cantor set in the three-sphere, where intersection numbers become counts of orbits of lifts. Along the way we show that commuting Dehn twists along primitive tori have tori whose lifts never cross, and that a Dehn twist determines the oriented cyclic splitting dual to its torus. Finally, we construct a compact space of primitive curves on which multitwists act parabolically and fully irreducible outer automorphisms act with north--south dynamics.

papers.title: On the class-breadth conjecture for $p$-groups
papers.abstract: The class-breadth conjecture of Leedham-Green, Neumann and Wiegold states that the nilpotency class of any $p$-group is at most $b(G) + 1$, where $\displaystyle{b(G) = \max_{g\in G}\log_p[G:Z_G(g)]}$ denotes the breadth of a group $G$. While several counter-examples to this conjecture have been found for $p = 2$, it is still open in general for $p > 2$. This article is dedicated to the general case $p > 2$ of the conjecture.

papers.title: From algebraic orthogonality to RAAG embedding obstructions in hierarchically hyperbolic groups
papers.abstract: We extend the Kim--Koberda obstruction arguments for embeddings of right-angled Artin groups (RAAGs) to a class of hierarchically hyperbolic groups (HHGs). To this end, we isolate algebraic conditions on HHGs relating domain orthogonality to the decomposition and commutation of group elements. Under these conditions, we obtain a clique-graph obstruction to RAAG embeddings into such HHGs using the \emph{expanded core graph}, which we introduce as a counterpart of both the extension graphs of RAAGs and the disjointness graphs of curves on surfaces. When the HHG structure has rank at most two, the expanded core graph itself gives a complete embedding criterion.

papers.title: Presentation of Borel subgroups of Kac-Moody groups over local rings
papers.abstract: We obtain presentations of Borel subgroups of certain Chevalley groups and Kac-Moody groups of simply laced type. More precisely, we show that Borel subgroups of simply laced Chevalley groups over a commutative, unital ring (satisfying a minor technical condition), are the amalgamated product of their rank 2 subgroups, generalising a result of Tits over fields (different from $\mathbb{F}_2$). We moreover show that Borel subgroups of Kac-Moody groups over local B\'ezout domains also have a presentation as an amalgamated product of their rank 2 subgroups as soon as this holds for their rank 3 subgroups. In particular we deduce that Borel subgroups of simply laced Kac-Moody groups over a local B\'ezout domain (with residue field different from $\mathbb{F}_2$) have such a presentation if and only if they are of 3-spherical type.

papers.title: Minimal Alt(6)-modules with additive dimension on characteristic not 3
papers.abstract: This article takes place in the extension and generalization proposed by Corredor, Deloro and Wiscons of the works of Dickson and Wagner regarding the Classification of minimal $\text{Sym}(n)$- and $\text{Alt}(n)$-modules. In particular, we classify the minimal faithful $\text{Alt}(6)$-modules with an additive dimension in characteristic not 3. We also highlight the remaining work needed to complete the classification of minimal faithful $\text{Alt}(n)$- and $\text{Sym}(n)$-modules with an additive dimension.
